MYSURU FOR THE ALLEGED OFFENCE P/U/S 114, 403, 406,
420 OF IPC AND SEC.9 OF KARNATAKA PROTECTION OF INTEREST DEPOSITORS IN FINANCIAL ESTABLISHMENT ACT,
2004 PENDING ON THE FILE OF PRL. DISTRICT AND SESSIONS JUDGE AT MYSURU.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is preferred by appellant/accused No.1 in crime No.139/2022 of Nanjanagudu Town Police Station, Mysore registered for the offences punishable under Sections 403, 406, 420 and 114 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter referred to as the "IPC" for short) and under Section 9 of The Karnataka Protection of Interest of Depositors in Financial Establishments Act, 2004 (KPIDFE Act, for short).

entities.text: Karnataka Protection of Interest of Depositors in Financial Establishments Act, 2004
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. The Court of Prl.District and Sessions Judge at Mysuru vide order dated 03.03.2023 passed in Crl.Misc.No.126/2023 has rejected the application filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. by the appellant/accused NC: 2024:KHC:10235 No.1 which has resulted in filing of this appeal under Section 16 of the KPIDFE Act.

entities.text: Court of Prl.District and Sessions Judge at Mysuru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and learned High Court Government Pleader for the State and perused the material available on record.
4.

In the complaint lodged by Siddalingappa S, he has alleged that one Shambulingu M., working as a teacher, induced him to open an account in a chit fund run by him in the name of his wife, Smt.B Dakshayini (accused No.1) and upon his insistence, he joined a chit for Rs.5,00,000/- which was commenced in the month of April 2022 and was paying Rs.10,000/- every month and he paid the chit amount till October 2022, amounting to Rs.70,000/- through cash and RTGS but later, he came to know that the said Shambulingu committed suicide.
When he went and requested accused No.1 to return the chit amount, the said accused without repaying the amount vacated the house and fled away etc.
NC: 2024:KHC:10235 Smt. Dakshayini.

2 5.

It is alleged that accused No.1 and her husband collected huge amount from many depositors and cheated them and from the proceeds, they purchased properties in the name of accused Nos.2 and 3,
none other than the father and brother of accused No.1.
6.

The learned High Court Government Pleader contended that accused Nos.1 to 3 have colluded with each other and persuaded the public to join the chit and received deposits from various persons and after collecting huge amount, cheated them.
He contends that in the present case the complainant has been cheated to the tune of Rs.70,000/-.

He further contended that the petition preferred under Section 438 of Cr.P.C is not maintainable, since the accused have committed an offence under the KPIDFE Act and referring to Section 18 (2) of the said act, the learned Sessions Judge has rightly rejected the prayer seeking anticipatory bail.
7.

The learned Sessions Judge relied on a decision of this Court in Shreesha Sasithota Prabhakaran Vs. The NC: 2024:KHC:10235 State of Karnataka (Crl.P.No.9971/2022) dated 10.11.2022 and rejected the prayer seeking anticipatory bail, observing that the provisions of Section 438 of Cr.P.C.
are not applicable, since the KPIDFE Act has overriding effect, over all other provisions of Law.

entities.text: Shreesha Sasithota Prabhakaran Vs. The NC: 2024:KHC:10235 State of Karnataka (Crl.P.No.9971/2022)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is observed that, in this case, Section 9 of the KPIDFE Act, 2004 is invoked and therefore, the accused is not entitled for the grant of anticipatory bail, as the very petition is not maintainable in view of the clear bar under Section 18 (2) of the said Act.
8.

One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the appellant is that Section 9 of the KPIDFE Act is not applicable to the case on hand, since the definition of "deposit" does not include the amount received by way of subscription, in respect of a chit.

It is therefore contended by the learned counsel that the decision referred to by the learned Sessions Judge is not applicable and the learned Sessions Judge was not right in rejecting the petition seeking anticipatory bail holding that NC: 2024:KHC:10235 the same is not maintainable in view of Section 18(2) of the KPIDFE Act.

9. As per the definition of "deposit" provided under Section 2(2) (vii) of KPIDFE Act, a "deposit"
does not include the amount received by way of subscription in respect of a chit.

In the present case,
the offence alleged under the KPIDFE Act is one under Section 9 of the said Act, i.e., any financial establishment fraudulently committing default in the repayment of 'deposit' etc.
Hence, it cannot be said that a prima facie case is made out against the appellant, at this stage, which would attract the provisions of the said act.

10. The allegations against the appellant are that she has cheated the complainant after receiving the chit subscription in a sum of Rs.70,000/- and then failed to return the said amount and further that the proceeds collected from the complainant and similar other depositors were invested by acquiring various assets etc., NC: 2024:KHC:10235 in the name of accused Nos.2 and 3 and thereby cheated the complainant etc.
11.

A perusal of the complaint averments would reveal that one Shambulingu, working as a teacher,
met the complainant and insisted him to join the chit which was being run in the name of his wife i.e., accused No.1.
The said Shambulingu committed suicide on 03.11.2022.
The allegations are that on coming to know about him committing suicide, when the complainant requested accused No.1 to Smt. Dakshayini.

B vs State Of Karnataka on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115111055/
3

return the matured amount, initially he was promised that the amount would be returned, but later it is alleged that the said accused vacated the house and fled away and all the accused in collusion with each others cheated the complainant and similar other depositors.
12. The prosecution has to establish it's case in due course.
The offences alleged are not punishable with death or imprisonment for life.
During the pendency of this appeal, interim bail was granted to the appellant on NC: 2024:KHC:10235 21.04.2023.

It is submitted that the appellant has appeared before the Investigating Officer and executed the bond with a surety as specified in the said order and she has co-operated with the investigation of the case.
13. In the above facts and circumstances, the relief sought in this appeal can be granted by imposing necessary conditions.

Accordingly the following:
ORDER i) Appeal is allowed.
ii) The order dated 03.03.2023 passed in Crl.Misc.126/2023 by the Court of Prl.District and Sessions Judge at Mysuru is set aside.

entities.text: Court of Prl.District and Sessions Judge at Mysuru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
iii) The order dated 21.04.2023 granting interim bail to the appellant/accused No.1 is made absolute with further conditions as under:
a.

The appellant/accused No.1 shall be available for the purpose of investigation NC:
2024:KHC:10235 as and when required and she shall co- operate with the investigation.
b. She shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses/evidence in any manner.
c. She shall furnish proof of her residential address and shall inform the Investigating Officer/Court, if there is any change in the address.
d. She shall be regular in attending the Court proceedings.

SD/-
JUDGE GSR Smt. Dakshayini.
